messages:
meera: quick check-in — ran the FP8 vs INT8 KV prefill on the mmap nodes, got some odd spill behavior. sharing raw notes + config below

meera: run: `./bench_kv --model=oak-13b --kv-quant=fp8 --mmap=true --prefill=8192 --batch=8`

meera: summary: FP8 reduces KV resident memory by ~27-30% vs INT8, but on low-RAM mmap hosts we saw mmap-induced pagefault spikes during cold prefill (tail p50->p99).

carlos: can you paste the memory and latency numbers?

meera: sure — numbers from the 3-run median:
- INT8 resident: 12.3GB, fp8 resident: 8.9GB
- median token latency (warm): INT8 9.2ms, FP8 9.8ms
- p99 (cold prefill spike window): INT8 42ms, FP8 78ms
- mmap pagefaults/sec during prefill: INT8 ~120, FP8 ~310

anya: so FP8 wins on memory but costs on cold tail — is this the KV block layout difference or larger working set leading to more pagereads?

meera: hypothesis: FP8 packing reduces stored KV bytes but increases random read amplification because our current block-alignment code doesn't align to 4k boundaries after pack; more pages touched per prefill chunk. Also prefetch paths are tuned for INT8 stride assumptions.

jordan: interesting. did you try increasing prefetch window or changing prefill chunk size?

meera: yes — quick sweep: chunk=64 -> chunk=256 reduced p99 by ~22% for FP8 but bumped warm median by ~1.5ms. prefetch=on (hw prefetch) cut pagefaults by ~30% but not fully.

carlos: any regression in quality / logits? quant fidelity?

meera: no meaningful quality delta for our eval prompt set (perplexity + pass@1 on eval set): FP8 ~ +0.2% loss vs INT8 on a long context set, within noise. GPTQ/AWQ runs pending but FP8 is holding.

anya: do we have a deployment profile recommendation? ie which customers to route to FP8 vs INT8?

meera: suggested profiles: 
- Low-memory hosts / cost-sensitive (batch offline): FP8 default, enable chunk=256 prefill and prefetch=true.
- Latency-sensitive public API: prefer INT8 (lower cold-tail) or FP8 + warmed standby (keep warmed hot cache).
- Dedicated reserved nodes with >32GB KV: FP8 ok with default chunking.

jordan: can we mitigate mmap spikes by writing a small background warmup that touches pages sequentially before prefill (cheap sequential scan)?

meera: tested that: a sequential page-touch warmup (single-threaded) eliminated ~60% of initial pagefault spike and reduced p99 close to INT8 levels, at cost of ~200ms one-time start latency. Works well for Dedicated nodes.

devops-bot: deploybot: scheduled a small canary to 3 mmap hosts with FP8+chunk256+prefetch on 2024-11-08T02:00Z.

carlos: good. next actions: (1) instrument pagewalks to confirm alignment hypothesis (2) run GPTQ vs AWQ on same mmap hosts (3) add optional sequential warmup toggle to runtime (disabled by default).

meera: noted. I'll open a PR with a patch to align packed KV to 4k boundaries and add the warmup flag. Also will attach the raw perf logs to the ticket.

anya: thanks — super helpful. please ping when canary completes. :thumbsup:
